name: c’wn annwn

attributes.attribute: are the hounds of the Welsh Otherworld
can take the form of ordinary beagles
range through the world baying in terrifying voices

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Welsh mythology tells of the c'wn annwn, named also cwn annwfn. These hounds belonged to the Welsh Otherworld. Like many fairy creatures they were red with white ears. They could also take the form of ordinary beagles. Their actions set them apart from normal dogs. They roamed widely, howling in ways that terrified hearers. People read their presence as a sign of coming death. The reader is directed to the entries Black Dog and Gabriel Hounds.

okr.objective: The c'wn annwn are the hounds of the Welsh Otherworld.
key_results: The c'wn annwn, also called cwn annwfn, were hounds of the Welsh Otherworld.
Like many fairy creatures they were red with white ears.
They could look like ordinary beagles but bayed in terrifying voices.
Their presence was believed to portend death.
